paragraphs: Cherries are photographed in pairs because of the stem. Two fruit joined at the top is the shape everybody recognises, and a single cherry with a cut stalk looks wrong in a way most people cannot immediately explain.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the fruit as static pieces. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 the set suits food and grocery visualisation, packaging and menu imagery, advertising, kitchen and market scenes, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2018.

A folded umbrella is a completely different object from an open one, and it is the state it spends almost all its life in. The strap, the point and the way the fabric wraps around the shaft are the details that make it read as put away rather than broken.
The model holds 36,354 polygons and 34,844 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in the folded state. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits product and accessory visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, character accessories, interior and street scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

Cleaning products are designed to look like they work. Bright colours, transparent bottles showing the liquid, and trigger sprays that feel decisive: almost none of it affects the chemistry, and all of it affects what gets bought.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the supplies as static pieces. It is built to CheckMate specification, and a second volume of the set is offered separately.
At $39 it suits product and packaging visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, interior and utility scenes, advertising, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A climbing helmet protects against what falls rather than against falling. The shell is designed for rock coming down from above, which is a different loading entirely from a cycling helmet, and it is why the shape and the harness are so different.

The model is light at 29,672 polygons and 29,814 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 6 maps all at 4096x4096, in a generic unbranded scheme. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits outdoor sports and equipment visualisation, e-commerce imagery, character accessories, safety material, game assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

The cordless handset was the last domestic telephone anybody designed, and it is now mostly a period marker: a house with one on the wall is being placed in a specific decade whether the production intended that or not.
The model is very light at 6,184 polygons and 6,565 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits interior and period visualisation, product and e-commerce imagery, film and television sets, game environments, advertising and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

Biological samples are stored at temperatures where nothing happens at all, chemically speaking. The boxes inside are a filing system in three dimensions, and every one of them has to be found in the seconds before the cold starts leaving the open door.
The model holds 100,042 polygons and 51,846 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied with the cryo boxes. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits laboratory and biotech visualisation, medical equipment marketing, research interiors, training material, film sets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2023.

A populated rack is the visible part of everything that happens online. Rows of identical units, cable management down one side, and a front that is nothing but airflow, because the compute itself has no appearance worth designing.
The model holds 128,753 polygons and 124,386 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits data centre and IT visualisation, hardware and infrastructure marketing, technical documentation, server room scenes, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2024.

The faux trophy is a joke about a tradition, and it works because the silhouette is unmistakable while the material never is. It hangs in bars and flats belonging to people who would not have the real thing on any account.
The model is extremely light at 3,820 polygons and 3,789 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, textured with 12 maps all at 2048x2048. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits interior and decor visualisation, product and e-commerce imagery, bar and hospitality scenes, film set dressing, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2020.

A tool belt is a filing system worn on the hips. Every pouch has a fixed occupant, the arrangement is personal and never discussed, and a belt covered in dust is one that has been organised by use rather than by the catalogue photograph.
The model is very light at 11,266 polygons and 11,705 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in dusty condition. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits construction and trade visualisation, tool and workwear marketing, character accessories, e-commerce imagery, film props and game environments. On sale since 2022.

Herb infused water is a presentation decision rather than a recipe. The dill has to be visible through the glass, arranged so it reads as fresh rather than as floating debris, and that arrangement is most of the work in any drinks photograph.
The model holds 236,334 polygons and 191,472 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is what the herb geometry requires. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits food and beverage visualisation, hospitality and menu imagery, advertising, kitchen and table scenes, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

An educational robot has to be a toy first or nobody finishes the tutorial. This one is a driveable platform with a camera and a programming environment behind it, and the whole design rests on being fun before it is instructive.
The model is built at subdivision level, 8,788 polygons and 9,290 vertices with non-overlapping UVs, so it smooths cleanly. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits education and technology visualisation, toy and product marketing, e-commerce imagery, classroom scenes, game assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2021.

A laser designator is a very expensive way of pointing. Somebody on the ground holds an invisible spot on a target while something else entirely does the work, and the whole device is built around keeping that spot steady for far longer than a human arm wants to.
The model holds 50,907 polygons and 52,022 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in tan. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits defence visualisation, equipment marketing, training material, character accessories, film props, game assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

A window robot has to hold on. Suction keeps it against the glass and a safety line catches it if the power fails, which is a design constraint no floor robot has ever had to think about, and the reason the category stayed small.
The model is light at 35,659 polygons and 37,431 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $39 it suits product and appliance visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, interior and facade scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

A full shavings bin is the detail that makes the object true. An empty sharpener is a product photograph; one with a pencil in it and curls of wood behind the window is a desk that somebody actually works at.
The model is dense at 618,614 polygons and 619,771 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, because the shavings are real geometry. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $39 it suits office and interior visualisation, stationery product imagery, e-commerce and advertising work, classroom scenes, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.
